target_audience: High school AP Calculus or first-year university students

sections.title: The Mystery of the Tangled Curve
lecture_lines: Explicit functions like parabolas are easy to differentiate.
But some curves have x and y locked together.
Even when tangled, we can find the curve's slope.
animations: Display the explicit function y = x^2 in #00FF00; a point moves along the parabola like a drone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drone.svg].
The parabola fades; the implicit circle x^2 + y^2 = 25 appears in #00FFFF with a 'locked' symbol over the 'y'.
A point (3, 4) appears on the circle; a short tangent line segment in #FFFF00 appears and pulses.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Secret Identity of 'y'
lecture_lines: Think of y as a box containing x.
Inside the box, y is a function of x.
Differentiate the outer layer using the power rule.
Then multiply by the inner derivative, dy dx.
This chain rule gives us the full result.
animations: A large box [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg] labeled 'y' in #FF00FF is shown; a label 'y is a function of x' appears.
The box opens (scales up/fades) to show a nested structure like a doll [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/doll.svg], representing y(x).
The term d/dx[y^3] appears; the 'outer' derivative 3y^2 is written in #FFA500.
The 'inner' part dy/dx appears in #FF0000 and multiplies the outer derivative.
The full result 3y^2 * dy/dx is highlighted with a surrounding glow effect.

sections.title: The Step-by-Step Recipe
lecture_lines: Follow these four steps to solve implicit equations.
Sort dy dx terms to the left side.
Factor out dy dx and solve for the slope.
animations: A vertical list of 4 steps appears on the left: 1. Diff, 2. Chain, 3. Collect, 4. Factor, next to the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/recipe.svg] icon.
A symbolic representation: blue blocks (non-dy/dx) and red blocks (dy/dx) are sorted to opposite sides of an '=' sign.
The red blocks are grouped, and a single dy/dx is factored out and highlighted in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Graphical Deep Dive: The Circle's Slope
lecture_lines: Let's find the slope on this circular path.
Differentiate both sides with respect to x.
Move terms without dy dx to the right.
Divide to isolate dy dx as the derivative.
Plugging in coordinates gives the tangent's exact slope.
animations: The equation x^2 + y^2 = 25 and its circle graph are shown; point (3, 4) is highlighted.
The derivative 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0 is animated in, with 2y(dy/dx) colored #FF0000.
The term 2x slides to the right of the equals sign, changing sign to -2x.
The equation is solved for dy/dx = -x/y, which is boxed in #00FF00.
The value -3/4 is calculated; the tangent line on the graph extends and its slope is displayed.

sections.title: The Interaction: The Product Rule Trap
lecture_lines: Multiplying x and y requires the product rule.
Use the derivative of the first times the second.
Add the first times the derivative of the second.
Combine all the differentiated terms into one equation.
Isolate dy dx to find the final derivative formula.
animations: The equation x^2 + xy = 10 appears; the term xy is highlighted in #FFA500.
The Product Rule formula f'g + fg' appears briefly as a guide.
The derivative of xy is shown: (1)(y) + (x)(dy/dx), with dy/dx in #FF0000.
The full equation 2x + y + x(dy/dx) = 0 is displayed.
The terms 2x and y move to the right side, leaving x(dy/dx) isolated on the left.

sections.title: Application: The Solar Orbit
lecture_lines: Elliptical orbits guide planets and space probes.
Implicit differentiation calculates their exact velocity direction.
This avoids messy square roots in complex trajectories.
animations: An ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 is drawn with a planet icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/planet.svg] orbiting it.
At a point on the orbit, a velocity vector (tangent line) in #00FF00 is drawn and follows the planet [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/planet.svg].
The formula for dy/dx for the ellipse appears; the tangent vector flashes to emphasize its importance for trajectory.
